report.title: Generic hull roll reduction with a U-tube anti-roll tank: screening estimate

code.install: none: clone the repository; no package install is needed

inputs.description: Leg length 20 m, leg width 6 m, fill depth 5 m, centroid offset 5 m, conduit area 6.8 m2, effective conduit length 5.2 m, density 1025 kg/m3, loss coefficient 2.389, loss area exponent 2.1381, bare-roll reference 5 deg, hull periods 18 s and 21 s, hull damping 2 % and 5 %, alpha 0.02 to 0.20
inputs.source: digitalmodel builder script and public U-tube model (all ASSUMED on the study page)

missing_data.what: A real hull: roll period, roll damping (% of critical), roll restoring and the tank's place and size
missing_data.why: The study uses a generic normalized hull; no real hull data is public.
missing_data.how_to_supply: Give the roll period, damping ratio and restoring; alpha is the tank's quasi-static moment stiffness divided by the hull's roll restoring.
missing_data.effect: None on the published result; needed to adapt it.

missing_data.what: The 35 CFD cases behind the tank moment fit
missing_data.why: They are published as aggregate results only.
missing_data.effect: The fit can be used but not rebuilt.

cannot_do: Rebuild the tank moment fit from the 35 CFD cases (aggregate results only).
Validate the estimate against a real vessel: no model or full-scale test is cited.
Give a design value: it is a screening estimate on invented geometry.

results.label: Peak roll reduction, 18 s hull roll period, 2 % hull damping, alpha 0.02
results.page_ref: Study page Figure 5.3 and Table A.1
results.period: one regular-wave sweep, 0.7 to 1.3 times the roll period
results.source: digitalmodel generic hull roll screening, data file docs/api/cfd/data/generic_hull_roll_screening.json (generated 25 October 2026)
limits: Generic normalized hull: no real hull mass, inertia or restoring is used.
Screening estimate on invented tank geometry; engineering review pending; no real-vessel test backs it.
The tank moment fit is validated for forcing periods of 20 s and longer; the 18 s results lie below that band.
